# NPM Improved v1.2.0

NPM Improved v1.2.0 introduces **NPMX (NPM Improved Exchange)**, a safer and easier way to pair and synchronize multiple NPM Improved servers, and adds cluster-aware Default Site templates.

## NPMX secure pairing

Primary/Secondary synchronization no longer requires administrators to invent, type, or manually copy a long-lived shared secret.

The Primary can now create a **one-time NPMX pairing code**. The code expires after 10 minutes and can only be used once.

During pairing, NPMX uses:

- ephemeral X25519 key exchange;
- HKDF-SHA256 key derivation;
- AES-256-GCM protected credential exchange;
- HMAC-SHA256 pairing proofs.

The persistent cluster credential is generated automatically, stored locally with restricted permissions, and is not displayed in the normal UI.

## Authenticated node-to-node exchange

After pairing, NPMX requests are authenticated without sending the cluster secret as a normal HTTP header.

Each request signature covers:

- protocol version;
- sending node ID;
- timestamp;
- random nonce;
- HTTP method and request path;
- canonical request-body digest.

Receivers reject stale timestamps, reused nonces, invalid signatures, and incompatible NPMX protocol versions.

## Capability negotiation

Before a Secondary accepts a synchronization snapshot, it negotiates NPMX protocol/version and required capabilities with the Primary.

NPMX v1 synchronizes the operational state required for another NPM Improved node to serve the same proxy configuration, including:

- Proxy Hosts and HA upstream pools;
- Redirection Hosts and 404 Hosts;
- Streams;
- Access Lists;
- users, permissions, authentication, and 2FA state;
- settings;
- certificates and certificate records;
- Let's Encrypt state;
- custom SSL assets;
- custom Nginx assets;
- Default Site templates;
- Configuration History and related cluster state.

The existing safety model is preserved: one authoritative Primary, read-only synchronized Secondaries, and controlled failover promotion.

## Cluster-aware Default Site templates

Custom Default Site HTML and redirect destinations can now use reusable variables.

Available values include:

- `{{node.hostname}}`
- `{{node.name}}`
- `{{node.id}}`
- `{{node.role}}`
- `{{node.public_url}}`
- `{{node.version}}`
- `{{node.build_commit}}`
- `{{node.build_date}}`
- `{{cluster.enabled}}`
- `{{cluster.protocol}}`
- `{{cluster.protocol_version}}`
- `{{system.platform}}`
- `{{system.arch}}`
- `{{system.generated_at}}`

NPMX synchronizes the **template**, not an already-rendered page. Each node renders its own local values, so the same Default Site can identify which proxy node actually answered a request.

The built-in fallback page has also been rebranded for NPM Improved.

## Restore reliability

v1.2.0 fixes restore handling for persistent Docker bind mounts such as `/etc/letsencrypt`.

NPM Improved now replaces the contents of mounted directories without attempting to remove the mount point itself. This applies to NPMX synchronization and disaster-recovery restore paths.

## Validation

The release adds integration coverage that starts two real NPM Improved containers and verifies:

- Primary/Secondary NPMX pairing;
- one-time credential exchange;
- matching persistent cluster credentials;
- encrypted snapshot synchronization;
- protocol/capability negotiation;
- node-local Default Site rendering on both nodes.

## Updating

Normal single-node v1.1.0 installations can install v1.2.0 from **Settings → Update** after the release appears as the latest stable version.

Instance Synchronization and Shared MySQL deployments remain coordinated-maintenance updates so participating nodes do not run mismatched application/schema versions.

Stable images are published for Linux amd64 and arm64:

```text
ghcr.io/gigabytegrove/npm-improved:v1.2.0
ghcr.io/gigabytegrove/npm-improved:1.2.0
ghcr.io/gigabytegrove/npm-improved:latest
```
